summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of COPD, atrial fibrillation, prior CABG, and alcohol abuse was admitted for evaluation of shortness of breath, chest pain, and new right lower back pain. Initial labs showed a mild leukocytosis and thrombocytopenia, with a slightly elevated d-dimer, but troponins were negative and imaging showed no pulmonary embolism or acute cardiac event. The shortness of breath was determined to be at baseline, with a possible minor aspiration event suggested by lab changes and a patulous esophagus on CT, though no pneumonia or COPD exacerbation was confirmed. The back pain was attributed to a muscle strain. He remained in paroxysmal atrial flutter but asymptomatic, with no need for changes in management. He was discharged home on his prior medications with a short course of low-dose oxycodone for back pain and counseling on smoking cessation.
